title: Intel chief says White House will not meddle in its semiconductor business
source_used: Nikkei Asia (lead paragraph and subhead only) plus a LavX News summary of the interview
key_facts: Nikkei Asia: Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said, in an exclusive interview, that the Trump administration does not have 'any policy' to use its minority stake in Intel to interfere in the company's business strategy.
Nikkei's subhead: Tan defends the Trump stake and assesses chips from China as not far behind US tech.
Nikkei caption: the US government, SoftBank Group and Nvidia have all taken equity stakes in Intel to support its recovery.
LavX summary: the US stake is about 8.2 percent after dilution from a secondary offering in August; the government bought in last year as a passive investment with no board seat.
LavX summary: Tan said 'They don't have any influence on the governance of the company' and that Intel is '80% done' with restructuring.
LavX summary: on China catching up in five to ten years, Tan said 'Today, I think it's not that far behind.'
quote_evidence: U.S. President Donald Trump's administration does not have "any policy" to use a minority stake in Intel to interfere in the chipmaker's business strategy, the company's chief executive said in an exclusive interview with Nikkei.
Lip-Bu Tan defends Trump stake, assesses chips from China as not far behind US tech
In an interview in Tokyo on Oct. 7, Tan said Washington's 8.2% holding carries no governance influence.
why_it_matters_hint: The CEO's own account of how far the government's stake reaches.
event_date: Nikkei published 16 Oct 2026; LavX dates the Tokyo interview to 7 Oct 2026 (unconfirmed)
notes: Nikkei Asia is paywalled: only the lead and subhead were readable. The rest comes from a LavX News summary (news.lavx.hu), an aggregator, so details such as the 8.2 percent stake and the interview date of 7 Oct are single-source and unconfirmed by Nikkei. Interview date not used in the summary.
